nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, $a_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} e_k p^k$, where $e_k$ is the $k$-th term of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$, read as a natural number.
nodes.title: Approximations as truncations of the p-adic expansion

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, $a_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} d_k p^k$, where $d_k$ is the $k$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$.
nodes.title: Approximations as sums of p-adic digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, $a_{n+1} = a_n + e_n p^n$, where $e_n$ is the $n$-th term of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$, read as a natural number.
nodes.title: One-step reconstruction from the p-adic expansion

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th $p$-adic digit $d_n$ of $a$ satisfies $a_{n+1} = a_n + d_n p^n$.
nodes.title: One-step reconstruction from p-adic digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. If two $p$-adic integers $a, a' \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ have the same $n$-th $p$-adic digit for every $n \ge 0$, then $a = a'$.
nodes.title: $p$-adic digits determine a $p$-adic integer

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. For every sequence $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers with $b_n < p$ for all $n$, there is a $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ whose $n$-th $p$-adic digit is $b_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Existence of a $p$-adic integer with prescribed digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. For every sequence $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers with $b_n < p$ for all $n$, there is exactly one $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ whose $n$-th $p$-adic digit is $b_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of $p$-adic integers with prescribed digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$ is strictly less than $p$.
nodes.title: p-adic digits are less than p

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th $p$-adic digit $d_n$ of $a$ satisfies $d_n p^n = a_{n+1} - a_n$.
nodes.title: p-adic digits measure the gaps between approximations

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. The $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$ is the natural number $(a_{n+1} - a_n)/p^n$.
nodes.title: Digits of a p-adic integer

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. The map sending a $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ to its $p$-adic expansion is a bijection from $\mathbb{Z}_p$ onto the set of all sequences $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with values in $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic expansion map is bijective

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. If two $p$-adic integers $a, a' \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ have the same $p$-adic expansion, then $a = a'$.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic expansion map is injective

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. Every sequence $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with values in $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$ is the $p$-adic expansion of some $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic expansion map is surjective

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th term of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$, read as a natural number, is the $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$.
nodes.title: Terms of the p-adic expansion are the digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. The $p$-adic expansion of $a$ is the sequence whose $n$-th term is the $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$, viewed as an element of $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$.
nodes.title: p-adic expansion

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
